title: Balanced Centered Heading

illustrates.quote: Divide a long centered heading at a logical break, balancing the two (or more) lines rather than dividing it arbitrarily.

blocks.text: USING NATURAL RESOURCES IN THE UNITED STATES
blocks.features: Bold black small caps, one long centered heading spanning the full width of the boxed print page; too long for one print line but shown here as the single heading being divided/balanced across two braille lines.

print.notes: Illustrates dividing a long centered heading across two lines at a logical break point ('...Natural Resources' / 'in the United States'), balanced rather than divided arbitrarily, per rule 4.4.3.
print.printFeatures: Boxed, centered, bold, full-capitals serif heading spanning the full width of the box; no accompanying body text shown in this excerpt.

braille.notes: Line 1 blank; line 2 'USING NATURAL RESOURCES' (whole-word capitalization indicator on each word) individually centered; line 3 'IN THE UNITED STATES' individually centered beneath it, division falling at a natural phrase break; line 4 blank.

resolution: braille.lines agree; text resolved to full capitals ("USING NATURAL RESOURCES IN THE UNITED STATES", matching run B) per the double-comma whole-word-capitalization indicator on every word in the braille -- run A's title-cased text does not match its own agreed braille.
